detect.note: PKHeX doesn't check the signature. The engine's hack formats claim saves signed their own way before PKHeX reads them, which the signature stands in for here.

pk3.note: A stored Pokémon after pk3-crypt, its substructures in the order Growth, Attacks, EVs and Condition, Miscellaneous.

ranges.name: Original trainer ID (TID low, SID high)
EVs: HP, Attack, Defense, Speed, Sp. Atk, Sp. Def
Contest stats: Cool, Beauty, Cute, Smart, Tough, Sheen

pk3-party.note: A party Pokémon after pk3-crypt: the 80 stored bytes and the battle stats.

Trainer name
ranges.note: 7 characters (5 in Japanese saves) then 0xFF.

ranges.name: Pokédex mode
ranges.note: 1 when the National Pokédex is on.

ranges.name: National Pokédex magic byte
ranges.note: 0xDA when the National Pokédex is unlocked.

ranges.name: National Pokédex magic byte (FireRed and LeafGreen)
ranges.note: PKHeX maps it on every Gen 3 small block; Ruby and Sapphire don't check it.

ranges.name: Pokédex owned flags
ranges.note: Bit per National Dex number, species 1 at bit 0 of the first byte.

ranges.name: Pokédex seen flags
ranges.note: Bit per National Dex number. Mirrored in section 1 and section 4.

ranges.name: Money

ranges.note: Plain value; Ruby and Sapphire have no security key.

ranges.name: Berries pocket

ranges.note: PKHeX writes it alongside the seen flags in section 0.

ranges.name: Berry Blender RPM records
ranges.note: For 2, 3 and 4 players, in hundredths of an RPM.

ranges.name: Event flags
ranges.note: 2,304 flags. The eight badges are flags 0x807 to 0x80E.

ranges.name: Game stats
ranges.note: Plain value; Ruby and Sapphire have no security key.

ranges.name: Secret base decorations
ranges.note: One decoration ID per byte.

ranges.name: Secret base decoration positions
ranges.note: One byte per decoration.

ranges.name: Secret base team
ranges.note: Six Pokémon: PIDs (u32le) at +0x00, moves (u16le, four each) at +0x18, species (u16le) at +0x48, held items (u16le) at +0x54, levels (u8) at +0x60, EV bytes (u8) at +0x66.

ranges.name: Secret base team (part 1)
ranges.note: The eighth base's team runs on into section:3.

ranges.name: Secret base decorations
ranges.note: One decoration ID per byte.

ranges.name: Secret base decoration positions
ranges.note: One byte per decoration.

ranges.note: Six Pokémon: PIDs (u32le) at +0x00, moves (u16le, four each) at +0x18, species (u16le) at +0x48, held items (u16le) at +0x54, levels (u8) at +0x60, EV bytes (u8) at +0x66.

ranges.name: Mail words
ranges.note: Nine easy chat words, u16le each. Slots 1 to 6 are the party's held mail.

ranges.name: Daycare Pokémon
ranges.note: Encrypted like a box Pokémon.

ranges.name: Roamer contest stats: Cool, Beauty, Cute, Smart, Tough
Mystery event script checksum
ranges.note: The low 16 bits of the sum of the script's bytes. Emerald uses a CRC instead.

ranges.name: Mystery Event script
ranges.note: The rest of the 0x3EC-byte script after its header. Its checksum covers it.

ranges.name: Pokédex seen flags (copy 3)
ranges.note: PKHeX writes it alongside the seen flags in section 0.

ranges.name: Hall of Fame trainer ID
ranges.note: 50 entries of 6 members, 20 bytes per member, run on from sector 28 into sector 29.

ranges.note: 50 entries of 6 members, 20 bytes per member, run on from sector 28 into sector 29.

seen-copy-2.note: The game counts a species as seen only when all three copies have its flag.

seen-copy-3.note: The game counts a species as seen only when all three copies have its flag.

is-egg.note: egg-and-species-flags at 0x13 has an is-egg bit too.

hatch-counter.note: An egg keeps its hatch counter in the friendship byte.
